persistent_identifier_status: Repository-local stable identifier; source DOIs are recorded per row.
title: Cross-technology literature and pilot benchmarks for drying energy
dataset_license: CC BY 4.0 for GreenHub-created metadata and unit conversions; original source rights and licenses remain with their respective publishers.
scope: Five reference records for thermal spray-dryer energy, a semi-technical juice spray-drying experiment, generic freeze/sublimation energy, a cultivated grass-clover pilot biorefinery, and a wheatgrass LCA inventory.

source_records.source_title: Energy Consumption of Industrial Spray Dryers
source_records.source_location: Abstract; journal pages 365–386. Survey commissioned by the UK Energy Efficiency Best Practice Programme.
source_records.license: Publisher copyright; no open license identified on the publisher record. Only attributed bibliographic metadata and reported summary values are represented here.
source_records.applicability: Technology-level spray-dryer comparator across food, chemical, and ceramic industries; evaporative capacity 0.1–12 t water/h. Not specific to grass protein or a GreenHub equipment design.
source_records.measurement_basis: Reported specific energy consumption 3–20 GJ/t water evaporated; survey mean 4.87 GJ/t, equivalent to 3–20 and 4.87 MJ/kg water evaporated.
source_records.uncertainty: Published range is retained as a range; the survey mean is not a probability distribution or GreenHub prediction.
source_records.conversion_and_scaling: 1 GJ/t = 1 MJ/kg by mass-unit conversion; no process scale-up or material correction applied.
source_records.provenance_note: Value is not used as the active GreenHub dryer default.

source_records.source_title: Spray Drying of Chokeberry Juice—Antioxidant Phytochemicals Retention in the Obtained Powders versus Energy Consumption of the Process
source_records.source_location: Section 3.4 and Figure 7, journal PDF pages 8–9 of 15.
source_records.applicability: Semi-technical spray drying of chokeberry juice with maltodextrin carrier; different matrix from GreenHub protein curd.
source_records.measurement_basis: Specific energy consumption 8,364–10,524 kJ/kg water evaporated over inlet air temperatures 150–185 °C; source Figure 7 reports point values and error bars.
source_records.uncertainty: Source reports measured variation/error bars; this CSV preserves the reported span and does not infer a distribution.
source_records.conversion_and_scaling: 1 kJ/kg = 0.001 MJ/kg; source values converted to 8.364–10.524 MJ/kg water evaporated.
source_records.provenance_note: Not used as an active GreenHub dryer default; feed formulation and equipment differ.

source_records.source_title: Sustainability of drying technologies: system analysis
source_records.license: Open-access article; publisher-specific reuse terms apply. No source text or table image is redistributed.
source_records.applicability: Review range for freeze/sublimation drying across source studies and materials; not specific to grass-protein curd.
source_records.measurement_basis: Table 1 lists 4.72–11.67 kWh/kg extracted water for freeze/sublimation drying.
source_records.uncertainty: Review-synthesized literature range; source studies and dryer boundaries differ, so it is not a GreenHub design interval.
source_records.conversion_and_scaling: Original kWh/kg extracted-water basis retained; no conversion or scale-up applied.
source_records.provenance_note: Not used as an active GreenHub freeze-drying energy value.

source_records.source_title: Environmental impacts of a biorefinery integrated into dairy farming system
source_records.source_type: peer-reviewed pilot biorefinery LCA with pilot-derived process inventory
source_records.source_location: Methods, biorefinery energy-demand paragraph; pilot energy inventory per Mg dry matter biomass.
source_records.license: Publisher article terms apply; no redistribution of article text or supplementary material in this dataset.
source_records.applicability: Cultivated grass-clover pilot biorefinery at Tuv, Norway; closest grass-biorefinary context in this set but not GreenHub roadside grass or its isoelectric route.
source_records.measurement_basis: Reported 138 MJ propane heat per Mg dry matter biomass for protein-concentrate drying; denominator is biomass DM, not water evaporated.
source_records.uncertainty: Pilot inventory value; no uncertainty interval or dryer-only water-evaporation balance identified in the cited text.
source_records.conversion_and_scaling: Original MJ/Mg DM basis retained. Not converted to MJ/kg evaporated water because a matched evaporated-water quantity and boundary are unavailable.
source_records.provenance_note: Do not use as a specific dryer duty without matching the route, material, and evaporation boundary.

source_records.source_title: A life cycle assessment of protein production from wheatgrass: Optimization potential of a novel vertical farming system
source_records.source_location: Table 3, drying heat input for 1 kg protein-concentrate powder.
source_records.license: Publisher article terms apply; no redistribution of article text or supplementary material in this dataset.
source_records.applicability: Vertical-farmed wheatgrass with membrane-based protein concentration; not roadside grass or an isoelectric curd drying test.
source_records.measurement_basis: Table 3 reports 2.7 kWh heat per kg protein-concentrate powder as an LCA inventory input.
source_records.uncertainty: Inventory point value; not reported as a direct dryer-metered SEC or water-evaporation-based efficiency.
source_records.conversion_and_scaling: Original kWh/kg powder basis retained; no conversion to energy per kg water evaporated.
source_records.provenance_note: Contextual route-level comparator only; not used as an active GreenHub dryer default.

data_management: All observations preserve their original denominators or report a transparent unit conversion. The dataset is reference-only and is not loaded as an active dryer scalar. Literature quality and GreenHub transferability are separate fields.
limitations: No record provides a complete direct energy-and-mass balance for GreenHub roadside-grass isoelectric protein curd drying.
The freeze/sublimation literature range is a review synthesis across materials and equipment; it is not a grass-protein operating setpoint.
The Elshani pilot value is per Mg dry feed and cannot be converted to energy per kg evaporated water without a matched evaporation mass and dryer boundary.
The wheatgrass value is an LCA process inventory per kg powder, not a direct meter reading or transferable water-specific dryer efficiency.
